title: AI that fits the way work actually runs.
lede: A practical synthesis of enterprise patterns from the 2025-2026 AI Annual Report: start with a real workflow, ground the model in business data, and keep people in the decisions that matter.
sourceNote: This page is a working synthesis of the report, not a reproduction or a timeless tool ranking. Vendor names and point-in-time predictions age quickly; the operating lessons travel further.

principles.label: Workflow
principles.title: Design a workflow, not a chatbot.
principles.body: The strongest cases connect input, interpretation, action, and follow-up. The model is one part of a process with an owner, an output, and a next step.

principles.label: Data
principles.title: Make business data usable first.
principles.body: Standard fields, shared definitions, clean records, and a dependable knowledge base matter more than a clever prompt. Data readiness is part of the AI product.

principles.label: Control
principles.title: Automate the repeatable; keep judgment visible.
principles.body: AI can handle retrieval, classification, drafting, and rule-based checks. High-impact decisions, exceptions, and uncertain outputs still need a named human owner.

principles.label: Adoption
principles.title: Let domain experts shape the system.
principles.body: The people closest to the work know the edge cases, the language, and the quality bar. Their participation turns AI from an imposed tool into a useful teammate.

cases.label: Recruiting
cases.title: Close the loop from first message to human decision.
cases.body: The report describes an AI recruiting workflow that configures role goals, screens candidates, communicates, schedules interviews, writes back to the system, and hands off at the moments that need a person.
cases.evidence: Reported signal: 24/7 coverage and 70-80% interview attendance when human reminders stay in the flow.
cases.takeaway: Enterprise lesson: measure the whole journey, not one automated message.

cases.label: Finance
cases.title: Standardize the source before automating the books.
cases.body: A finance team first unified its source table and field definitions, then used AI, formulas, code, and RPA to compare, map, and route the work. The automation was built around a clearer data model.
cases.evidence: Reported signal: invoice preparation moved from 3 people over 3 days to 1 person for half a day; sensitive fields were masked and outputs were checked.
cases.takeaway: Enterprise lesson: automation becomes safer when the input contract is explicit.

cases.label: Legal
cases.title: Move from document review to process visibility.
cases.body: The legal case followed a durable sequence: put contracts online, standardize reusable clauses, then use AI for first-pass review and drafting. Workflow timing and bottlenecks became visible alongside the text.
cases.evidence: Reported signal: AI reduced repetitive review work while legal review remained mandatory; process data made cycle time and late signing easier to manage.
cases.takeaway: Enterprise lesson: the lasting value is often the operating model around the model.

cases.label: CRM
cases.title: Start with the customer record people can actually use.
cases.body: A lightweight CRM combined a shared customer record, interaction history, voice-to-field capture, reminders, dashboards, and personalized follow-up. The design favored familiarity and adoption over technical novelty.
cases.evidence: Reported signal: 70-80% of routine work could be delegated, while the final customer touch and data checks stayed with people.
cases.takeaway: Enterprise lesson: the best AI layer is often the one users do not have to learn from scratch.

cases.label: Manufacturing
cases.title: Turn expert judgment into a feedback loop.
cases.body: The quality-inspection case connected consistent image capture, a labeled defect library, on-site inference, expert review, and continued model improvement. Frontline specialists became coaches rather than spectators.
cases.evidence: Reported signal: a shift from sampling to full inspection, with reported throughput near 50,000 parts per hour and accuracy around 95%.
cases.takeaway: Enterprise lesson: explainability and expert participation are adoption infrastructure.

cases.label: Decision support
cases.title: Build a data hub before a multi-agent layer.
cases.body: The water-management case connected multiple data sources, a domain knowledge base, small specialist workflows, and a routing layer. The architecture made it easier to know which tool was responsible for which question.
cases.evidence: Reported signal: routine reporting and analysis accelerated, while high-impact warnings and public-safety decisions stayed under human review.
cases.takeaway: Enterprise lesson: higher autonomy needs stronger routing, provenance, and escalation rules.

sequence.title: Name the work
sequence.body: Choose one painful, frequent workflow with a clear owner and a visible business outcome.

sequence.title: Define the input
sequence.body: Agree on fields, source systems, permissions, context, and what counts as a good result.

sequence.title: Shape the handoffs
sequence.body: Break the work into small steps and decide what the model may do, suggest, or never decide.

sequence.title: Measure the outcome
sequence.body: Track cycle time, quality, adoption, exceptions, rework, and business impact - not speed alone.

sequence.title: Learn in the flow
sequence.body: Use real exceptions, user feedback, and expert review to improve the workflow one iteration at a time.

watchouts.label: Do not start with
watchouts.title: A giant AI program
watchouts.body: A small, high-frequency use case gives the organization evidence and trust before the scope expands.

watchouts.label: Do not assume
watchouts.title: The model fixes bad data
watchouts.body: Inconsistent records, unclear ownership, and scattered knowledge will show up as unreliable outputs.

watchouts.label: Do not hide
watchouts.title: The human checkpoint
watchouts.body: Make review, escalation, auditability, and responsibility explicit wherever the cost of error is high.
